facts.text: Totah Vista's name blends the Navajo word 'Totah,' meaning 'between the waters,' pointing to the angle where the San Juan, Animas, and La Plata rivers meet.
Totah Vista sits just east of Navajo Nation lands, highlighting the enduring indigenous influence in the area.
At 5,282 feet above sea level, Totah Vista enjoys a high desert setting that shapes its climate.
The semi‑arid climate brings hot July highs around 91°F and cold January lows near 18°F, with about 14 inches of snow yearly.
After the Ancestral Puebloans left circa 1300 CE, Athabaskan groups, including the Navajo, settled the area, bringing a semi‑nomadic pastoral lifestyle.
In the 1990s and 2000s, Totah Vista grew alongside regional oil and gas expansion, prompting infrastructure upgrades tied to San Juan County's Capital Improvement Plan.
